drhp.business: Jaiprakash Power Ventures is engaged in thermal and hydro power generation supported by coal mining and cement grinding. It owns and operates three power plants aggregating 2,220 MW, selling power to state distribution companies under long-term PPAs and the balance as merchant power on exchanges and bilateral basis. Its captive coal mine feeds the Nigrie thermal plant, while its cement-grinding unit remained idle and is being positioned for exit.
drhp.end_markets: State distribution companies (UPPCL, MPPMCL)|Government of Madhya Pradesh and Government of Uttarakhand|Merchant power buyers via Indian Energy Exchange, Hindustan Power Exchange and Power Exchange of India|Madhya Pradesh|Uttarakhand
drhp.expansion: Jaiprakash Power Ventures owns and operates three power plants with an aggregate capacity of 2220 MW, a 2 MTPA Cement Grinding Unit and a 3.92 MTPA coal mine. The generating assets are the 400 MW Vishnuprayag Hydro-Electric Plant in Uttarakhand (in operation since October 2006, 88% supplied to UPPCL under PPA and 12% free to the Government of Uttarakhand), the 500 MW (2x250 MW) Jaypee Bina Thermal Power Plant at Sirchopi, District Sagar, Madhya Pradesh (units commissioned August 2012 and April 2013, 70% of installed capacity tied to MPPMCL long-term with the balance sold as merchant power), …

litigation.note: An application under Section 7 of the IBC was filed before NCLT Allahabad by NARCL to initiate CIRP against the company over a corporate guarantee it extended to Jaiprakash Associates Limited, with a similar matter pending before DRT-III Delhi; the company is contesting these claims and considers them not maintainable. Separately, the Non-Executive Chairman Shri Manoj Gaur is under judicial custody in an ED/PMLA investigation relating to Jaypee Infratech and Jaiprakash Associates, which the company states has no impact on its operations. BSE and NSE also levied fines for alleged non-compliance with Regulation 17(1A) of SEBI LODR regarding the appointment of an Independent Director over 75 years of age.

risks.note: MPPMCL gives restricted, erratic and fluctuating dispatch schedules to Bina TPP, sometimes scheduling very low offtake, which renders it technically unfeasible to run the plant optimally and forces the Company to sell balance power on exchanges at un-remunerative tariffs.
risks.risk: Erratic offtake / restricted dispatch by MPPMCL at Bina TPP

risks.note: A large share of Nigrie and Bina generation is sold as merchant power on energy exchanges and bilateral arrangements (e.g. 5,799.24 MUs merchant sales at Nigrie), leaving realizations exposed to volatile short-term power market prices rather than long-term PPA tariffs.

Vishnuprayag Hydro Electric Power Plant generation is dependent on river flows; FY26 generation was lower than the prior year due to hydrology, making this run-of-river asset's output structurally weather/monsoon dependent.
risks.risk: Hydrology dependence at Vishnuprayag hydro plant

risks.note: Post year-end the Board decided to surrender the Amelia (North) and Bandha North coal mines citing recent changes in Government coal policies, economic viability and sociological aspects; the surrender is subject to requisite approvals and affects the captive coal linkage that fed Nigrie plant.
risks.risk: Surrender of captive coal mines / coal supply security

risks.note: Increasing renewable generation reduces daytime power demand from thermal plants, forcing thermal machines to operate at lower generation to meet SLDC/WRLDC schedules, which creates stresses in the boiler-turbine-generator (BTG) systems.
risks.risk: Flexible operation stress from rising renewables

risks.note: Thermal operations require significant water and generate effluent, ash and hazardous waste; non-compliance with water discharge, Zero Liquid Discharge and waste standards carries regulatory penalties, environmental liabilities and reputational risk.
risks.risk: Environmental and water compliance (ZLD, hazardous waste, emissions)

risks.note: Difficulty obtaining spares or support for equipment and systems installed at the time of plant commissioning is flagged as a risk, mitigated by maintaining sufficient spares, in-house repair strength and technology upgrades.

Cyberattack is flagged as a global threat to major industrial organizations including generating plants; the Company relies on GoI requirements and a Group CISO monitoring internal and external factors.

sk.overview: The Indian corporate/C&I renewable power market covers solar, wind and wind-solar-hybrid power procured by commercial and industrial consumers via open-access, group-captive, third-party PPAs and increasingly virtual PPAs (VPPAs/EAPAs) and energy-attribute certificates (I-RECs). C&I consumers account for over 50% of India's power market; renewable energy offers 30-45% cost savings over grid tariffs, driving substitution of grid power with bilaterally-procured renewables under a supportive open-access regulatory regime.

sk.structure: C&I renewable procurement via onsite solar, offsite STU-connected (group captive / third-party open access), CTU/ISTS-connected, and virtual PPAs (VPPA/EAPA with I-RECs). Distinct from utility-scale developers who bid lowest-tariff tenders to state discoms; C&I model is customer-specific …
